panels.description: Insertion of the next dyadic neighborhood between previously constructed closures and open neighborhoods.

entries.description: An arrow links a shaded unit square, whose top and bottom edges are labeled y=1 and y=0, to a shaded irregular image in the coordinate plane.

panels.description: The domain [0,1] x [0,1], with its two distinguished horizontal edges.
The planar image of an extension of the two boundary paths.

panels.description: Finite partitions of a closed interval used as a directed set for integration.

panels.description: Metric neighborhoods of a maximal separated subset, with V the complement of the union of smaller closed neighborhoods.

entries.description: The real interval from 0 to 1 contains a marked interior point u, surrounded by a shaded, bracketed open-cover element U_i.

panels.description: An open neighborhood extends a finite cover beyond a proposed supremum in the proof of compactness of [0,1].

entries.description: One cluster of overlapping irregular neighborhoods covers a shaded compact set A; a second, separate cluster has a shaded common neighborhood around the external point x.

panels.description: Finitely many open neighborhoods cover the compact set A.
Intersection of matching neighborhoods gives a neighborhood of x disjoint from A.

entries.description: The cylinder I×C has solid boundary ellipses labeled {1}×C and {0}×C. The upper left point x marks the interval fiber I×{x}; 1 and 0 mark the interval endpoints at the right.

panels.description: The compact cylinder obtained as the product of a circle and [0,1].

entries.description: A torus is drawn with its central hole and dashed hidden portions, and leaders label circle fibers from its two product factors.

panels.description: Compactness of the product of two circles, represented by a torus.

entries.description: The wireframe cube I×I×I has vertically hatched first-coordinate-zero face {0}×I×I and diagonally hatched third-coordinate-one face I×I×{1}. Vertical stripes continue into a triangle on the top, and a bent leader points left into the first face. The front left vertical edge is marked 0 and 1.

panels.description: The compact product [0,1]^3 is represented as a cube.

panels.description: A bounded subset A of Euclidean space lies inside the closure of a product neighborhood of the origin.

panels.description: A compact closed metric neighborhood fits inside any prescribed neighborhood of x.

entries.description: A horizontal real line has an open interval (a,b), the rational point x, an irrational point t, and an overbrace indicating containment in the interior of A.

panels.description: The interval used to construct an open cover contradicting local compactness of the rational subspace.

entries.description: An oval ambient space X contains a crosshatched diamond-shaped subspace Y, a small irregular neighborhood around point y, and leaders marking relative and ambient open sets.

panels.description: Local compactness of Y is related to its being open in its closure.

entries.description: An arrow maps a detached point A={-1} and a positive half-line B into a coordinate plot with the point (0,0) and the rapidly oscillating curve y=sin(1/x).

The image combines (0,0) with the oscillating graph (x,sin(1/x)) for x>0.
